title: Compact polyglot on-ramps: CLI + server walkthroughs for Next.js, FastAPI, Go
creator: Priya Nair
description: Create a small, focused set of polyglot example projects that demonstrate best-practice SDK usage patterns: minimal Next.js app for web client/server, FastAPI server example for Python backends, idiomatic Go HTTP server, and a CLI reference demonstrating idempotent retries, streaming consumption, and graceful shutdown. These on-ramps should be tiny (single-file or minimal repo) so engineers can copy-paste into a new project and run locally. Aim for reproducible CI checks that validate core behaviors (retry semantics, streaming offsets, and example smoke tests).
background: We get repeated questions from early adopters about how to wire retries, streaming handlers, and cancellation semantics into common stacks. Existing sample packs are comprehensive but heavy; we need compact, opinionated examples that show one recommended pattern per stack. This will lower onboarding time and reduce support churn.
tasks: Design minimal example layout and README for each stack
Implement Next.js example (edge and serverless flavors) with client-side streaming and server proxy patterns
Implement FastAPI example showing streaming generator, context manager for connections, and retry wrapper
Implement Go example using net/http with graceful shutdown and tokenized retry middleware
Implement CLI example (Python) that demonstrates resumable streaming with checkpoint files and exponential backoff
Add lightweight CI smoke tests for each example (start app, call endpoint, assert response shape)
Publish examples to examples.redwood.dev and add links in SDK quickstart docs
decision_log: 2025-02-11: Decided to standardize retry semantics across SDKs: idempotent GET-like requests should use fast retries; generation requests use conservative backoff. See design notes.

2025-02-12: Choose streaming ergonomics: Python exposes iterator + context manager, TypeScript exposes async iterator with optional onData callback, Go exposes channel-based scanner with Close() for cancellation.
2025-02-14: Opted to keep examples minimal (no auth integrations) and point to a separate enterprise example for KMS/SSO to avoid scope creep.

acceptance_criteria: A single-file or single-folder runnable example for each stack (Next.js, FastAPI, Go, CLI) with clear README
Examples demonstrate recommended retry patterns (configurable) and have at least one unit/integration smoke test
Streaming examples expose ergonomic consumer APIs (iterator/async-iterator/channel) with cancellation semantics documented
CI pipeline runs and passes smoke tests on merge
Links to examples are added to SDK quickstart and onboarding checklist
notes: Keep examples small. Include explicit TODOs to point users at the more advanced Dedicated/Private deployment patterns. Ensure README explains when to use each pattern (low-latency vs throughput).
